claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.

In a CodePipeline pipeline using the default `SUPERSEDED` mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, if enough commits land while the stage is busy, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (pipelineType V2).
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set the pipeline's `executionMode` and `pipelineType`.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link target /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists as the API docs page for the `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource.
When two pipeline runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
The Pulumi docs have an update-conflicts troubleshooting page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from deploying at the same time.
The Azure DevOps approvals-and-checks documentation at learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals covers the exclusive lock check.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines YAML supports a stage-level `lockBehavior` property that controls how a stage interacts with an exclusive lock check on the environment it references.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` stage property is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is evaluated against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time.
The Azure DevOps Pulumi provider has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
The Pulumi Registry has an API docs page for the azuredevops CheckExclusiveLock resource at /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` running a Pulumi update.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity build configuration option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that the deployment job targets serializes Pulumi deployments so they do not overlap.
In Azure Pipelines, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` is used together with an exclusive lock check on the environment so that queued runs proceed sequentially.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'Serialize deployments with an exclusive lock' (anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock).
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
In AWS CodePipeline, the default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'Serialize pipeline executions' (anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions).
In TeamCity, setting the build configuration option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 serializes Pulumi deployment builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'Limit concurrent builds' (anchor #limit-concurrent-builds).
